provenance.citation: Elastic corneoscleral FEM (no remodeling; spec §7). The stress-free geometry is found by a fixed-point inverse solve so that the IOP-only state is the document's geometry, and the result is the change from that state (--reference measured instead takes the document as stress-free). Stiffness calibrated to the in-vivo ocular rigidity (data/materials). The loads other than IOP act as a linear perturbation of the pressurized eye (the nonlinear solve softens under the full muscle load, an artifact of the support model). Approximations: fixed optic-nerve support; muscle forces from length-proxy activation x capacity, brought into static equilibrium with a linear passive orbital moment by the least change, with the net force and the passive moment taken by an orbital reaction on the orbit's posterior hemisphere; lid bands fixed in the orbit at the lid margins; dead loads in the reference configuration; Zernike maps fitted within 4 mm of the axis; lens follows the scleral spur, the cornea is measured relative to the spur ring's lateral shift and tilt, and the retina follows the edge of the optic-nerve support. Materials, thickness, eyelid, and force data are unverified (see data/materials, data/eyelid, data/eom). Tests the hypothesis that muscle and lid loading shape the cornea; not an established result.

frame: right eye, origin at the globe center (taken as the center of rotation, an approximation), x temporal, y superior, z posterior (toward the retina), mm

scleralMaps.projection: stereographic about the posterior pole from the anterior pole, rho = 2R tan(alpha/2), alpha the angle from the posterior pole, equator at rho = 2R; azimuth atan2(y, x) in the FEM frame (x temporal, y superior)

reference.label: Navarro, Santamaría & Bescós 1985 accommodation-dependent schematic eye (regression fixture)

provenance.citation: Navarro R, Santamaría J, Bescós J. Accommodation-dependent model of the human eye with aspherics. J Opt Soc Am A 2(8):1273-1281, 1985. Table 1 (relaxed surfaces, indices) and Table 4 (accommodation dependence).

params.note: Viewer defaults, assumptions: binocular viewing of a 60° × 60° adapting field (a room-sized scene).

lensAccommodationModel.description: Lens and anterior chamber as functions of accommodation A (diopters), Table 4. L = ln(1 + A). anteriorRadius = R_a0 + anteriorRadiusPerLn * L; posteriorRadius = R_p0 + posteriorRadiusPerLn * L; thickness = t0 + thicknessPerLn * L; anteriorChamberDepth = ACD0 + chamberDepthPerLn * L; index = n0 + indexCoeff * (10 A + A^2); anteriorConic = Q_a0 + anteriorConicPerLn * L; posteriorConic = Q_p0 + posteriorConicPerLn * L. The retina stays at axialLengthMm and the vitreous absorbs the change in anterior chamber depth and lens thickness (buildSurfaces).
lensAccommodationModel.unverifiedNote: Radius, thickness, chamber depth, and index coefficients were confirmed against excerpts of Table 4 on 2026-10-26. The two conic coefficients could not be confirmed from the reachable excerpts and are retained from the secondary literature; confirm against the paper before relying on them.
